clue.text: WWII fighter pilot, holding king captive, used to make cakes

indicators.note: the pilot's name holds the other words inside it, as hands hold something

parts.note: Douglas Bader, the legless RAF fighter ace of the Second World War
taken as written
POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: A wartime flying ace takes a monarch prisoner, somehow in the service of baking.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas Bader was the famous RAF ace who flew despite losing both legs; his name is split open to take in the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Baking powder is the raising agent stirred into flour so that sponges and scones rise.

clue.text: Concocting half a breast and a wing

indicators.note: only half of the following word is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: taken as written, to be cut
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook prepares a dish from part of a chicken breast and a wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Brewing is preparing a drink or potion by mixing and steeping ingredients, hence concocting.

clue.text: Milk and one of two equal parts of rennet churned up in Russian citadel

indicators.note: churning stirs things up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

indicators.text: one of two equal parts of
indicators.note: one of two equal parts is a half, so only half of the word is kept

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be halved

explanation.surface: Milk and rennet are churned up in a Russian fortress, like cheesemaking in Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of RENNET is REN; with MILK that makes seven letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the walled fortress complex in Moscow, the seat of Russian government.

clue.text: It's dusk and a man is heard to drop

indicators.note: being heard means we take the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: a knight is a man in chess
to fall is to drop

explanation.surface: As evening falls, a man is heard dropping something.
explanation.walkthrough: A man in chess is a piece, and the knight is one; its sound gives the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is the time when darkness comes at the end of the day, the same as dusk.

clue.text: Attractive young woman to turn informer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lovely girl, in informal speech
second meaning: to betray accomplices to the authorities, an old slang verb

explanation.surface: A pretty young woman decides to become a police informant.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit names a pretty girl, and the unrelated old verb means to tell tales on a partner in crime.

clue.text: Wholemeal: how soon about to swallow?

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: when asks how soon
to swallow food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone asks how soon the wholemeal loaf will be ready to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheaten bread is made from whole wheat flour, so it is a wholemeal loaf.

clue.text: What's notable is mine preserved in elastic net

indicators.note: something preserved in another is kept inside it
something elastic stretches out of shape, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something remarkable is kept safe in a stretchy net.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent describes a person of distinction, someone famous and respected in a field.

clue.text: Winner has the courage to drink heavily

parts.note: a hit is a success
taken as written
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: The victor has the nerve to start drinking hard.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, having bottle means having courage.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the bottle is the idiom for starting to drink alcohol to excess.

clue.text: Master of "Titanic" in charge of bird turning tail

definitions.note: a cryptic description: the iceberg got the better of the ship

parts.note: IC is the usual abbreviation for in charge

indicators.note: turning tail means turning round, so the bird's name runs back to front

parts.note: the grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: Someone commands the Titanic while a bird flees from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' looks like the ship's captain, but the thing that mastered the Titanic was what it struck.
explanation.definitionFit: The liner sank in 1912 after striking a floating mass of ice, which thus overcame it.

clue.text: I'm continent in the morning; so I care to move

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon

indicators.note: the letters are told to move about and settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-controlled speaker announces they are restrained in the morning and so concerned to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continent' reads as self-restrained, but it is the landmass; the answer is talking about itself.
explanation.definitionFit: North and South America together are often called one continent, the landmass of the western hemisphere.

clue.text: Light meal, in style of almost nobody, to eat out

parts.note: a painting after Rembrandt is in his style

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: nobody is no one
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A light meal served in a style where hardly anyone eats out.
explanation.definitionFit: Afternoon tea is the British late-day snack of sandwiches, cakes and a pot of tea.

clue.text: Like baby needing holiday permit?

definitions.note: a triplet is a baby born with two others alike

parts.note: a trip is an outing or short holiday
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A baby seems to need a travel permit for its holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Triplets are three children from one birth, so each is a baby with two near-identical siblings.

clue.text: Wiggle toes in hat: an awkward position

indicators.note: one set of letters goes inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written, to be opened up

indicators.note: wiggling things moves them about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wiggles their toes inside a hat, which is certainly awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the hot seat is the idiom for being in a difficult place where you must answer for things.

clue.text: In novel, Gingerbread Man who collected marbles?

indicators.note: the letters sit in the following phrase, straddling its words

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A storybook Gingerbread Man is cast as a collector of marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: The marbles are not toys but the Parthenon sculptures, still called the Elgin Marbles in the British Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Elgin removed the Parthenon friezes from Athens in the early 1800s and sold them to Britain.

clue.text: Carpet tool rests against stone held by miner

indicators.note: one piece leans up against the next, so they sit side by side

parts.note: ax is the American spelling of axe

indicators.note: the stone is held inside the word for a miner

parts.note: taken as written, to be opened up
st is the abbreviation for the weight stone

explanation.surface: A miner's tool lies propped against a stone he is holding.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a type of woven pile rug named after the Devon town where it was first made.

clue.text: Doctor of Divinity divides up profit in riper years

indicators.note: dividing a word splits it open, with the other piece inserted in the gap

parts.note: to get mileage out of something is to profit from it
DD is the degree abbreviation

explanation.surface: A clergyman shares out his gains in his later years.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle age is the period of life between youth and old age, when one is more mature.

clue.text: Restyled red velour rejected

indicators.note: something restyled is given a new form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A redesign in red velvety fabric was turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A decision that is overruled is set aside by higher authority, so it has been turned down.

clue.text: Centre of well re-made meter is wooden

definitions.note: an adjective for a noun: an elm tree is made of wood

indicators.note: only the central letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the middle two letters

indicators.note: something re-made is put together differently, so its letters change order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebuilt water meter at the heart of a well turns out to be made of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: An elm tree is a large broadleaf hardwood, a thing made of timber, so the clue loosely calls it wooden.

clue.text: Not starting to be greedier, so thinner

indicators.note: not starting means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written, to be beheaded

explanation.surface: Refusing to grow greedier keeps you slimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedy means slender like a reed, so the comparative describes someone or something slimmer.

clue.text: Mexican snack for doctor outside a church

indicators.note: the doctor's name sits on the outside, wrapping round the rest

parts.note: Dr No, the villain of the James Bond film
taken as written
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A tortilla snack is bought for a doctor standing outside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor is not MO or DR but a particular one, the Bond villain Doctor No.
explanation.definitionFit: Nachos are crisp tortilla chips topped with cheese, a Tex-Mex dish.

clue.text: Bin overturned with small amount found in club

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so in a down entry the word reads the other way

parts.note: taken as written
a lick of paint is a small amount

explanation.surface: A tipped-over bin with a little rubbish is found in a club.
explanation.walkthrough: The club is a golf club, not a society.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old Scottish golf club with a lofted head, roughly a modern nine iron.

clue.text: Honesty demands unfinished candy belonging to us

indicators.note: unfinished means the end of the word is left off

parts.note: taken as written, to be cut short
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: A truthful child insists the half-eaten sweets are theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour is frankness and openness in speech, a plain form of truthfulness.

clue.text: Try to shield English MP in violent storm

indicators.note: to shield something is to surround and protect it, so one word wraps round the others

parts.note: to test is to try out
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to protect an English member of parliament during a fierce storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a literary word for a furious gale, as in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: This pound comes from the bottomless mug

indicators.note: with no bottom the word loses its last letter, its foot in a down entry

parts.note: taken as written, to be cut
to mug someone is to rob them

explanation.surface: A pound coin is found in the bottom of a mug with no bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money, but it is the verb for a heart beating hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb is to beat with strong regular pulses, which is what a pounding heart or head does.

clue.text: Coward takes in catch coming back in the Med

definitions.note: a description, not a synonym: a country on that sea

indicators.note: coming back means the whole thing runs in the opposite direction
the playwright's name takes another word inside it

parts.note: Noel Coward, the English playwright and wit
to nab is to catch

explanation.surface: A cowardly sailor makes a catch while returning across the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like a timid person, but it is Noel Coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a Middle Eastern country whose coastline lies on the eastern Mediterranean Sea.

clue.text: Nobleman that is right to appear more quickly

parts.note: an earl is a British peer
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A peer is told the correct thing is to show up sooner.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a sooner time, which matches arriving more promptly than expected.

clue.text: Fatty Labour girl goes back to model

indicators.note: going back means the girl's name runs backwards

parts.note: Ida is a girl's name; Labour seems only to dress the surface
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: A girl from the Labour Party heads back to work as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: IDA backwards gives ADI, followed by POSE; 'Labour' appears to add no letters and serves the political picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose is the technical adjective for body tissue that stores fat.

clue.text: Fickle lover having courage to wave

parts.note: to have heart is to have courage
a breaker is a wave crashing on the shore

explanation.surface: An unfaithful lover finds the nerve to wave goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wave' reads as a verb, but the wave is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartbreaker is someone who wins affection and then abandons partners, causing them grief.
